Phoenix to Sedona Transportation Guide

Red rock country awaits just two hours north of Phoenix. Whether you're planning a day trip, wine tour, or romantic getaway, here's everything you need to know about getting to Sedona in comfort and style.

Transportation Options Compared

Private Car Service

Best for: Couples, small groups, luxury experience

  • Door-to-door service from any Phoenix location
  • Professional chauffeur handles navigation
  • Climate-controlled comfort
  • Flexibility to stop for photos along the way

Sprinter Van

Best for: Groups of 8-14, wine tours

  • Comfortable captain's chairs
  • Room for coolers and purchases
  • One vehicle, one group
  • Cost-effective for larger parties

Self-Drive

Best for: Flexibility, multiple-day stays

  • Scenic route via I-17 North
  • Stop at Montezuma Castle, outlets
  • Park at various trailheads
  • Navigate unfamiliar mountain roads

Route Options

Via I-17 (Fastest - 2 hours)

The most direct route through Black Canyon City and Camp Verde. Exit onto AZ-179 for the scenic approach through Village of Oak Creek.

Via AZ-87 Beeline Highway (Scenic - 2.5 hours)

Through Payson and Pine, this route offers forest scenery but adds time. Best for those visiting Tonto Natural Bridge.

Day Trip Itineraries

Wine Lover's Day

  • 9:00 AM: Depart Phoenix
  • 11:00 AM: First winery (Page Springs Cellars)
  • 1:00 PM: Lunch at Merkin Vineyards
  • 3:00 PM: Second winery (Javelina Leap)
  • 5:00 PM: Sunset views at Airport Mesa
  • 7:00 PM: Return to Phoenix

Adventure Seeker's Day

  • 7:00 AM: Depart Phoenix
  • 9:00 AM: Hike Cathedral Rock
  • 12:00 PM: Lunch in Uptown Sedona
  • 2:00 PM: Jeep tour or vortex visit
  • 5:00 PM: Tlaquepaque shopping
  • 7:00 PM: Return to Phoenix

Romantic Escape

  • 10:00 AM: Leisurely departure
  • 12:00 PM: Brunch at Elote Cafe
  • 2:00 PM: Chapel of the Holy Cross
  • 4:00 PM: Spa treatment at Enchantment Resort
  • 6:00 PM: Sunset dinner at Mariposa
  • 8:30 PM: Return under the stars

Why Choose a Driver?

The drive to Sedona includes:

  • Winding mountain roads through Oak Creek Canyon
  • Wildlife crossings (deer, elk)
  • Limited cell service in some areas
  • Challenging parking in peak season

A professional driver handles these challenges while you enjoy the views.
